state.instructions: Use the included rules and code to judge the proposed version separation property.
state.facts: Existing notices and pre-arrival delivery use Booking.version as a material-change fence. A background producer that stores its progress on Booking would increment that fence and suppress valid messages. The proposal separates immutable booking purchase/charge identity, original allowance-overage money, billing place, product and attribution snapshot from mutable progress: CommercialSale is one child per Booking with phase and revision. In one bounded owner transaction the check selects or provisions that child, updates it only on a different phase, and emits original-source SaleMilestone. The provided language rule leaves an unwritten parent unchanged after a child write. Eligible paid evidence needs positive initial monetary_due, paid payment, confirmed/occupied/completed status, consumed/not_required allowance, clean cancellation/refund controls and collected/refunded proof; completion also needs actual departure. Cancelled/no_show/refunded cases become terminal reversed. Review/expired cases reverse a prior publication but do not fence a never-published sale from late-space recovery. Invoice still checks actual ledger money and trustworthy acquisition history itself. The existing reservation event triggers CommercialCheck through a bridge; newly covered invalidation branches queue only that check and do not resend notices. Same verified account/customer and selected latest_capture(customer,actor,location,product) authorize optional hour/day attribution. For quotes the accepted contract conveys four already-frozen origin values plus explicit product, validated against the owning resource.kind. No attribution is required for internal work. No cancellation_passed assertion follows from refund_before. Everything described is unimplemented target behavior.
state.actual_code:
A created row has version 1 throughout its creating transaction, including create-hook adjustments. Ordinary references to an existing row expose its admitted version `v` throughout the owner transaction while field reads observe ordered provisional changes. An accepted `set`, CRUD update or archive reserves `v+1`, even for a normalized same-value write. Further writes/calls/hooks to that row do not advance it again. Update-hook `event.before.version` is `v` and `event.after.version` is the reserved `v+1`; create-after is 1. Permanent removal has no after record; its deleted event carries `v+1`. A child write does not advance an unwritten parent. Failed operations advance nothing; receipt replay reapplies nothing. This write-intent rule intentionally produces history/version changes for accepted no-op writes. Locks compare stored values, not modification metadata.
